text:
Zach Werenski arrived at this season as the reigning Norris Trophy winner and an Olympic gold medalist, and he is still playing over 28 minutes a night for Columbus. The point totals look like his: 14 in 15 games and a six-game point streak, with a late equalizer against Dallas and a power-play goal in Buffalo in the last week.

The underlying picture is softer than the line. At five on five the Blue Jackets are almost exactly even in shots and expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 49%, and they have scored 6.9 more goals than those chances deserve. That is padding his assists, and on-ice luck like that usually fades. His own shot is quiet too: 2 goals on 43 shots.

Last season he was the opposite of quiet. Evolving-Hockey had him 4th among 215 defensemen at 3.8 wins above replacement, and his team created clearly more with him on. If that driving play comes back, the points will not need the luck. Watch whether the five-on-five share climbs above even.
headline: Werenski is piling up points on luck
